Title: Super Administrator bypasses recent step-up authentication
Attack Path: Steal or reuse the active local Super Administrator password/session; invoke a sensitive endpoint; the shared helper exempts Super Admin from recent step-up.
Impact: A single password/session compromise can become tenant-wide identity, payroll, document, or audit compromise without a second factor at the critical action.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Access Control; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Remove the Super Admin bypass; require fresh phishing-resistant Entra authentication or a separately controlled, vaulted, alerted, time-bounded break-glass process; revoke legacy sessions after rollout.
Acceptance Test: Sensitive endpoints reject stale/non-step-up Super Admin sessions; break-glass use emits a high-severity alert and immutable review record.
Target Window: Contain immediately; permanent fix within 30 days

Title: API connects to PostgreSQL as the postgres superuser
Attack Path: Exploit any API code-execution or database-access flaw; inherit database superuser authority; read or alter all HR data, roles, constraints, triggers, and audit state.
Impact: Application compromise becomes complete database compromise and materially weakens recovery and forensics.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Access Control and Operations; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Use the existing hr_erp_app role at runtime and a separate time-bounded migrator identity; grant only required schema, table, sequence, and function privileges.
Acceptance Test: Runtime current_user is non-superuser; API negative tests cannot create roles, disable triggers, or access unneeded schemas; migrations require the migrator.

Title: Plaintext backups and HR PDFs exist in operator and deployment directories
Asset: Database backups; generated payslips, profiles, settlements; operator OneDrive; VM filesystem
Attack Path: Compromise a synced workstation identity, stale host account, Docker-group principal, or local process; read 0644 backup files or read/modify generated PDFs, some mode 0666, outside application authorization and audit.
Impact: Bulk identity, payroll, banking, and document disclosure; document tamper; uncontrolled retention; breach-notification exposure.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Asset/Data/BCM; Law Arts. 8, 10, 13 and 14
Remediation: Inventory before deletion; securely remove unapproved copies after retention/legal approval; quarantine required copies in encrypted access-logged storage; enforce least-privileged ownership/modes; prevent generated documents in source roots.
Acceptance Test: Approved DLP/file inventory finds no raw SQL or employee PDF outside governed stores; deployment artifacts are non-sensitive; mode/ownership checks pass.
Target Window: Contain immediately; permanent fix within 30 days

Title: Security monitoring is incomplete and health metrics are stale or incorrect
Asset: Cloud Monitoring; Cloud Logging; Ops Agent; incident detection
Attack Path: An attack or control failure occurs while health signals are false/stale or the relevant privilege, audit, secret, malware, container, or exfiltration use case has no detection; responders miss or discount it.
Impact: Longer attacker dwell time, late breach discovery, weak reconstruction, and unreliable operational assurance.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Incident Management; Law Arts. 11 and 14
Remediation: Repair virtual-host-aware health probes; retire obsolete tunnel metrics; restore Microsoft-expiry telemetry; alert on freshness; implement and own missing security detections and runbooks.
Acceptance Test: Synthetic signals trigger the intended alert/channel within SLA; stale metrics alert; dashboards show current health; quarterly detection tests are recorded.
Target Window: Repair false health immediately; complete within 30 days

Title: Microsoft onboarding enables login before Entra object binding
Asset: Employee onboarding; email changes; Entra provisioning; Microsoft login
Attack Path: Create a corporate employee or change an existing employee to @med-tech.com; the application attempts microsoftLoginEnabled before an object ID is bound; the database rejects the invalid state and returns 500; retry/manual workarounds can orphan identities.
Impact: Denied Microsoft login, inconsistent lifecycle/revocation, orphaned Entra/local identities, and future misbinding risk if the constraint is weakened.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Access Control and Acquisition; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: For both new onboarding and corporate-email transition: provision or resolve Entra first, bind exact tenant/object ID, then enable Microsoft login; use one idempotent shared flow with compensation/rollback; retain the database constraint.
Acceptance Test: Tests cover both required flows, Graph failure, duplicate UPN/mail, retry, rollback, and wrong-object prevention; success can sign in; failure remains disabled with a controlled non-500 response.

Title: Production origin is directly exposed without the expected Cloudflare or WAF layer
Asset: DNS; public IP; Nginx; edge protection
Attack Path: Resolve and target the VM origin directly; bypass expected managed WAF, bot, or DDoS controls; attack the single host and application.
Impact: Greater automated-abuse and origin attack surface, with availability dependent on a single VM/application stack.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Communications and Operations; Law Art. 13
Remediation: Restore an approved Cloudflare/private-origin design or approve and harden the direct design with managed load balancing/WAF, origin restriction, rate controls, and monitored DDoS posture.
Acceptance Test: Origin is unreachable except through the approved edge, or compensating direct-origin controls and runbooks pass an external verification.

Title: Upload validation accepts content that does not match declared MIME type
Attack Path: Upload non-PNG bytes with an allowed PNG declaration; pass extension/declared-MIME allowlist and malware scan; later consumer handles the content differently.
Impact: Stored-content confusion, downstream parser exposure, unsafe sharing, and weakened document trust; nosniff and safe download behavior reduce immediate browser impact.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Operations and Application Security; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Detect file type from magic bytes/content; compare with declared MIME and extension; reject mismatches while preserving malware scan, quarantine, and safe headers.
Acceptance Test: Mismatch, polyglot, truncated, renamed, EICAR, and oversized fixtures are rejected or quarantined; valid formats still work.

Title: Container hardening, resource controls, and image provenance are incomplete
Asset: Docker Compose; web, API, ClamAV, PostgreSQL images
Attack Path: Compromise a container; use writable filesystem, excessive identity/capabilities, absent resource limits, or mutable images to persist, exhaust the host, or expand blast radius.
Impact: Availability loss and larger cross-service/host impact on the single production VM.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Operations and Communications; Law Art. 13
Remediation: Run non-root where supported; drop capabilities; add no-new-privileges, read-only roots/tmpfs, CPU/memory/PID limits, approved digest pinning, SBOM/provenance, and vulnerability gates.
Acceptance Test: Compose regression verifies controls; bounded load cannot starve PostgreSQL/host; deployment admits only approved digests.

Title: Release and security-baseline prefixes fall outside governed backup lifecycle
Asset: GCS backup bucket; releases; security baselines
Attack Path: Long-lived duplicate database, document, certificate, source, or screenshot artifacts accumulate outside hourly/daily/weekly/monthly lifecycle rules; a later bucket compromise exposes a larger historical set.
Impact: Larger breach scope and difficult retention, deletion, and data-subject obligation handling.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Asset Management, Data Protection and BCM; Law Arts. 8, 10 and 13
Remediation: Classify every prefix; prohibit PII, secrets, and screenshots in release artifacts; apply owned lifecycle/retention and test deletion/legal-hold behavior.
Acceptance Test: Every prefix has an owner, classification, maximum retention, lifecycle rule, and sampled content validation.

Title: Secret rotation and expiry governance is incomplete
Asset: Secret Manager; JWT; database; audit HMAC; recovery bootstrap; Microsoft credential
Attack Path: A long-lived secret leaks through a process, host, backup, or operator path and remains usable because age, overlap, rotation, and revocation are not consistently governed.
Impact: Prolonged unauthorized access and difficult containment; unsafe audit-HMAC rotation could also impair verification.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Cryptography and Access Control; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Define owner, maximum age, overlap, revocation, rollback, and monitoring per secret; automate where safe; preserve audit verification across HMAC rotation.
Acceptance Test: Inventory shows owner/purpose/last-next rotation; age and anomalous access alert; dual-version rollout and rollback tests pass.

Title: Entra governance lacks verified tenant-wide access policy and application owners
Attack Path: Compromise an administrator or application credential; no verified tenant-wide MFA/device/location/risk condition and no accountable app owner delays containment and renewal.
Impact: Identity compromise and application lifecycle gaps; Security Defaults remains Not Verified.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Access Control and Governance; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Assign at least two accountable owners per application; verify Security Defaults/Conditional Access; require phishing-resistant admin authentication; document break-glass exclusions; monitor credentials and consent.
Acceptance Test: Read-only evidence shows approved policies and protected populations; break-glass test passes; all applications have active owners.

Title: Administrative host access lacks OS Login 2FA and retains stale Docker-group users
Asset: GCE OS Login; SSH; sudo; Docker group
Attack Path: Compromise an eligible cloud identity/key or abuse/reactivate a stale Docker-group user; gain root-equivalent VM/container control without host-level 2FA enforcement.
Impact: Full host, container, database, and secret-access compromise.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Access Control; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Enforce OS Login 2FA/strong Conditional Access; validate owners then remove stale accounts and Docker memberships; alert on sudo/Docker administration.
Acceptance Test: No unowned local Docker users; interactive admin access requires strong MFA; quarterly access review exists.

Title: Tracked and installed edge configuration are not reconciled
Attack Path: A future deploy or rollback uses stale tracked Nginx configuration and silently removes live callback-log, routing, or default-deny hardening.
Impact: Security regression and non-reproducible recovery.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Configuration and Operations; Law Art. 13
Remediation: Reconcile installed configuration into source; retire obsolete variants after evidence retention; gate deployments on edge regression against the actual artifact.
Acceptance Test: Installed and tracked hashes match; all edge tests pass in CI and post-deploy verification.

Title: Twenty PostgreSQL constraints remain NOT VALID
Attack Path: Historical inconsistent rows remain latent; authorization, payroll, leave, or identity logic assumes integrity that was never validated.
Impact: Workflow or authorization errors, incorrect calculations, or migration outage.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Data and Application Security; Law Arts. 10 and 13
Remediation: Identify violations read-only; remediate under change control; validate constraints in bounded batches with rollback and monitoring.
Acceptance Test: Zero unintended NOT VALID constraints; integrity regression passes on restored production data before production validation.

Title: Supported dependency vulnerabilities remain in production and development graphs
Attack Path: A vulnerable parser, API documentation, PDF, build, or test dependency processes attacker-influenced input and triggers an advisory path.
Impact: Impact ranges from development compromise to server-side data or code impact; reachability remains to be proven per advisory.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Application Security and Operations; Law Art. 13
Remediation: Upgrade within compatible ranges, remove unused packages, run targeted reachability/regression checks, and time-bound documented exceptions.
Acceptance Test: Production and development audits are clean or each exception has owner, reachability evidence, compensating control, and expiry.

Title: Backend CSV exports do not neutralize spreadsheet formulas
Attack Path: Attacker-controlled text begins with a spreadsheet formula trigger; a privileged user opens the exported CSV; the spreadsheet interprets the cell as a formula or external interaction.
Impact: Operator workstation data exfiltration or unsafe link/command behavior depending on spreadsheet controls.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Application Security; Law Arts. 8 and 13
Remediation: Apply one server-side formula-neutralization rule before CSV quoting; preserve raw values in non-spreadsheet APIs.
Acceptance Test: Fixtures beginning with equals, plus, minus, and at-sign open as inert text in Excel and LibreOffice and round-trip safely.

Title: Internal PostgreSQL transport is not encrypted
Attack Path: Compromise another container or the host network plane; observe or manipulate internal database traffic that uses SCRAM but no TLS.
Impact: HR data and credentials could be exposed after an initial local compromise; loopback/Docker scoping reduces likelihood.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Communications and Cryptography; Law Art. 13
Remediation: Enable authenticated PostgreSQL TLS with client verification or document an approved equivalent-isolation exception with stronger segmentation and monitoring.
Acceptance Test: Clients verify the database certificate and reject plaintext, or an approved risk exception proves equivalent isolation.

Title: Security assurance scripts and lint are not consistently green
Attack Path: Security-sensitive behavior changes while stale or missing scripts create false confidence and the intended test never runs.
Impact: Higher probability of an authorization or configuration regression escaping review.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Governance and Application Security; Law Art. 11
Remediation: Repair or remove stale entry points; wire required suites to CI; make non-rewriting lint, build, and security commands deterministic.
Acceptance Test: One documented clean-checkout security command runs every intended suite and exits cleanly.

Title: Host discovery and agent listeners are broader than needed
Attack Path: A future firewall or local-network change exposes all-interface management/discovery listeners; an attacker gains discovery, spoofing, or agent attack surface.
Impact: Additional host attack surface; currently mitigated by GCP firewall denial.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Communications and Operations; Law Art. 13
Remediation: Disable unused LLMNR; bind agent endpoints to loopback where supported; keep listener/firewall regression checks.
Acceptance Test: Listener inventory contains only documented addresses/ports; external verification confirms denial.

Title: Default log retention and key management lack a documented policy decision
Attack Path: An incident is discovered after the 30-day default retention period or policy requires customer-controlled key revocation; detailed evidence is unavailable or key controls do not match policy.
Impact: Reduced forensics and potential policy mismatch; Required logs retain 400 days and are locked.
Qatar NIA 2.0 / Law 13 of 2016: NIA Incident Management and Compliance; Law Arts. 11 and 14
Remediation: Align retention per log class with detection/legal requirements; route high-value logs to controlled longer retention; adopt CMEK only if policy requires it.
Acceptance Test: Retention matrix, cost approval, access review, and historical search/recovery test are documented.
